commands.summary: Move or rename a file or directory

options.description: Overwrite an existing destination without prompting.
Prompt before overwriting an existing destination.
Do not overwrite an existing destination.

sections.heading: Description
sections.body: Moves a source path to a destination or renames it in place.

sections.heading: Risk
sections.body: May overwrite the destination or make the source unavailable at its old path.

commands.summary: Update timestamps or create empty files

arguments.label: FILE
arguments.description: Files whose timestamps should be changed.

options.description: Do not create files that do not exist.
Change only the access time.
Change only the modification time.
Use the specified date string instead of the current time.

sections.heading: Description
sections.body: Updates file access or modification timestamps and creates missing files unless disabled.

sections.heading: Risk
sections.body: Changes filesystem metadata and may create new empty files.

commands.summary: Print the first part of files

arguments.label: FILE
arguments.description: Files to read; standard input is used when omitted.

options.description: Print the requested number of lines.
Print the requested number of bytes.
Never print file-name headers.

sections.heading: Description
sections.body: Writes the beginning of each selected file or standard input.

sections.heading: Safety
sections.body: Reads input without modifying it.

commands.summary: Print or follow the last part of files

options.description: Print the requested number of final lines.
Continue reading as a file grows.
Keep trying to open an inaccessible file while following.

sections.heading: Description
sections.body: Writes the end of files and can continue streaming appended data.

sections.heading: Lifecycle
sections.body: Follow mode remains active until cancelled and should have explicit process controls.

commands.summary: Count lines, words, characters, or bytes

arguments.label: FILE
arguments.description: Files to count; standard input is used when omitted.

options.description: Print newline counts.
Print word counts.
Print byte counts.
Print character counts.

sections.heading: Description
sections.body: Prints selected counts for each input and a total when multiple files are supplied.

sections.heading: Safety
sections.body: Reads input without modifying it.

arguments.label: FILE
arguments.description: Text files to sort; standard input is used when omitted.

options.description: Reverse the comparison result.
Compare according to numeric value.
Output only one line for each equal run.
Use the specified field-separator character.

sections.heading: Description
sections.body: Writes a sorted merge of input lines to standard output.

sections.heading: Locale
sections.body: The active locale affects collation unless a locale is set explicitly.

commands.summary: Display used and available system memory

options.description: Show automatically scaled human-readable values.
Display memory in bytes.
Refresh continuously at the specified interval.

sections.heading: Description
sections.body: Reports physical and swap memory totals from the Linux kernel.

sections.heading: Lifecycle
sections.body: An update interval keeps the process running until cancelled.

commands.summary: Show system uptime and load averages

options.description: Show uptime in a human-friendly format.
Show the timestamp when the system started.

sections.heading: Description
sections.body: Shows the current time, elapsed uptime, logged-in user count, and load averages.

sections.heading: Safety
sections.body: Reads system accounting information without modifying it.

commands.summary: List block devices and filesystem information

options.description: Include empty devices.
Show filesystem-related columns.
Produce JSON output.
Select a comma-separated output column list.
Print only devices matching a libsmartcols filter expression (util-linux 2.40 or newer).

sections.heading: Description
sections.body: Reads sysfs and udev data to display block devices in a tree or selected format.

sections.heading: Safety
sections.body: Inspection options do not modify block devices.

arguments.label: SOURCE
arguments.description: Device, label, UUID, or remote filesystem.

arguments.label: DIRECTORY
arguments.description: Directory where the filesystem should be attached.

options.description: Mount filesystems described by fstab.
Limit or select filesystem types.
Use a comma-separated mount option list.
Mount the filesystem read-only.

sections.heading: Description
sections.body: Lists mounted filesystems with no arguments or attaches a filesystem to the directory tree.

sections.heading: Risk
sections.body: Attaching filesystems changes system state and usually requires elevated privileges.

options.description: Operate recursively on directories.
Report every processed file.
Report only files whose ownership changes.

sections.heading: Description
sections.body: Changes user and group ownership for selected paths.

sections.heading: Risk
sections.body: Incorrect ownership can expose data, deny access, or alter privilege boundaries.

sections.heading: Description
sections.body: Prints the user name associated with the current effective user ID.

sections.heading: Safety
sections.body: Reads process identity information without modifying accounts.

arguments.label: DESTINATION
arguments.description: Host name or address to probe.

options.description: Stop after sending the requested number of packets.
Wait the specified interval between packets.
Do not resolve addresses to host names.
Use IPv6 only.

sections.heading: Description
sections.body: Sends ICMP echo requests and reports reachability and round-trip timing.

sections.heading: Network
sections.body: Generates network traffic and may continue until cancelled unless a count is supplied.

arguments.label: COMMAND
arguments.description: Git subcommand such as status, log, clone, or commit.

options.description: Run as if Git was started in the selected directory.
Do not pipe output into a pager.
Set a configuration key for this invocation.

sections.heading: Description
sections.body: Dispatches version-control subcommands for inspecting or changing repositories and remotes.

sections.heading: Risk
sections.body: Read-only subcommands are low impact; reset, clean, checkout, commit, pull, and push can change local or remote state.

commands.summary: Inspect or modify the environment for a command

arguments.label: NAME=VALUE|COMMAND
arguments.description: Environment assignments followed optionally by a command and its arguments.

options.description: Start with an empty environment.
Remove a variable from the command environment.
Change to the selected working directory before running a command.

sections.heading: Description
sections.body: Prints the current environment or runs a command with an adjusted environment.

sections.heading: Risk
sections.body: When a command is supplied, env executes it; review both assignments and the full command arguments.

options.description: Decompress selected files.
Keep input files instead of deleting them after success.
Force compression or decompression and overwrite outputs when allowed.
Print compression information for each file.

sections.heading: Description
sections.body: Compresses files to gzip format or restores compressed files.

sections.heading: Risk
sections.body: By default successful compression or decompression replaces the input; use keep when preservation is required.

commands.summary: Run a command under another security identity

arguments.label: COMMAND
arguments.description: Command to execute with the selected security identity.

arguments.label: ARGUMENT
arguments.description: Arguments passed to the selected command.

options.description: Run the command as the specified user instead of root.
Run the command with the specified primary group.
Run the target user's login shell environment.
Preserve the calling environment subject to sudo policy.
Fail instead of prompting when authentication is required.

sections.heading: Description
sections.body: Executes a reviewed command under another user or group according to the local sudo policy.

sections.heading: Risk
sections.body: Privilege elevation is always High risk. Authentication stays inside the PTY and password input is never stored in application state, events, history, logs, or AI requests.
